video_title: "Il Canto dei Sanfedisti" - Cover by Jack Wale
description:
"Il Canto dei Sanfedisti" is a Neapolitan Folk Song which was born out of the turbulent year 1799, when the Kingdom of Naples was briefly overthrown by invading French revolutionary forces and replaced with the failed and short lived Parthenopean Republic. Sung by the Sanfedisti, "the Soldiers of the Holy Faith", this piece represents the voice of the common people and clergy in southern Italy who were lead by Cardinal Fabrizio Ruffo and rose up in armed resistance against the French armies to restore the monarchy, and to defend themselves against social upheaval, Jacobin atheism, and foreign occupation. This song, which is rich in satire and contemporary idiomatic expression, celebrates the uprising of the 'populo bascio' and mocks the republican elite who had attempted to impose enlightenment ideals upon a catholic society. The verses of this piece recounts the major events and sentiments of the Neapolitan Counter-Revolution of 1799. 

Behind the lyrical humour lies a serious reflection on loyalty, faith and cultural resistance. Despite it's modern popularity, this song was originally composed anonymously in the wake of Sanfedisti victory, and has survived through oral tradition and writing. Furthermore, it remains a rare window into the vernacular culture of early 18th century southern Italy, and stands out not only as a historical document of popular royalism and anti-revolutionary attitude, but as a folk anthem of resistance.

Thank you for watching my cover of this song, and my apologies for the delay in creating new music! Please forgive any mistakes in pronunciation or the written translation as parts of the English translation have been modified to keep meaning. I hope you enjoy!

video_title: "Á Sprengisandi" - an Icelandic Folk Song Cover by Jack Wale
description:
"Á Sprengisandi" is an Icelandic folk song, originally written by the author and poet Grímur Thomsen (1820-1896). The Sprengisandur was a passage route used during the times of the Icelandic Commonwealth (930 - 1265)  which was only accessible in the summer. It remained impassable in the winter due to ice and snow, and also in the spring due to heavy rain and flooding.

Sprengisandur gives the area its name which is derived from the Icelandic noun sandur "sand," which symbolises the volcanic ash deserts in the island's centre, and the verb sprengja, which means "to ride a horse to death".

I hope that you enjoy this cover of the song and please forgive any mistakes in pronunciation or translation!

video_title: "Ved Stanford Brua" - Cover by Jack Wale
description:
"Ved Stanford Brua" is a song originally written and sung by the Norwegian folk singer Harald Foss. It describes in poetic verse the events of the battle of Stamford Bridge in which King Harald Sigurdsson, better known in the English speaking world as King Harald Hardrada of Norway, was defeated by King Harold Godwinson of England and his army on the 25th of September, 1066. Many historians assert that the defeat of the Norsemen at the battle of Stamford Bridge marked the official closure of the Viking Age. This version of the song is the first digital cover to be made.

Harald Foss is a talented musician who has contributed much to the preservation of Norse and Norwegian history, the original version of the song can be found here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t_WGs2d3R74

Thank you for watching and please excuse any mistakes in pronunciation or translation!

description:

video_title: Mayhem Tribute - Freezing Moon  (Feat. Samoth, Gaahl, Trym, Snorre, Neddo) 2021
description:
Mayhem was inducted into the Norwegian "Rockheim Hall of Fame", which is similar to "Rock & Roll Hall of Fame" in the USA, in 2021.
There was a short ceremony, and other artists were paying tribute to Mayhem, playing cover versions of their songs.

This is one of those cover songs. It is the song "Freezing Moon", and the tribute band members are Samoth, Gaahl, Snorre Ruch, Trym and Neddo.

video_title: Coldplay - Hunting High and Low  (A-ha cover, Live in Norway, 2001, pro-shot)
description:
Coldplay frontman Chris Martin performing an acoustic version of the A-HA classic "Hunting high and low", originally released by the Norwegian band in 1985.
This performance is from the "Quart Festival" in Kristiansand, Norway, in July 2001. Possibly the earliest live recording of Coldplay doing this cover. At least on YouTube.
Originally recorded by myself from Norwegian TV, in 2001, onto a VHS cassette.
Credits to the now shut down TV-station "Metropol TV".

video_title: Parte de tu Mundo Cover (2002/2023 Castilian Spanish Version)
description:
ES:
¡Hola todos! Este ha estado sentado en mis borradores por un TIEMPO, pero estoy muy feliz de finalmente compartir con todos ustedes mi cover de "Parte de tu Mundo". Me sorprendió mucho durante MerMay2023 cuando se lanzó la versión oficial en español castellano de "Parte de Él" y me di cuenta de que iba a usar la letra original de Latino de 1989 y no la letra de Castellano de 2002. Como admirador de la traducción audiovisual, me encanta la variedad que ambas versiones ofrecieron al mundo hispanohablante y, sinceramente, me sentí tan triste que no pudiéramos escuchar a Mirela dar vida a esas letras de Castellano de 2002 en la película live action de La Sirenita. ¡Así que decidí hacerlo yo mismo! ¡Espero que todos disfruten!

P.D.

Aunque Mirela no llegó a cantar la letra de 2002 en la película de live action, ¡tiene un cover en vivo de esa versión que recomiendo! Échale un vistazo aquí: https://youtu.be/p4Yze9-A7-I?si=pIpQdrLtxs0zR07w


ENG:
Hi everyone! This one has been sitting in my drafts for a WHILE now, but I am so happy to finally share with you all my cover of “Parte de tu Mundo”. I was so surprised back in MerMay 2023 when the official Castilian Spanish version of “Parte de Él” was released and realized that it wpuld be using the original Latino 1989 lyrics and not the Castellano lyrics from 2002. As an admirer of audiovisual translation, I love the variety that both versions offered to the Spanish speaking world and was honestly pretty bummed that we wouldn’t get to hear Mirela bring those 2002 Castellano lyrics to life in the live action. So, I decided to do it myself! I hope you all enjoy!

P.S.

Although Mirela didn’t get to sing the 2002 lyrics in the live action, she does have a live cover of that version which I HIGHLY recommend! Check it out here: https://youtu.be/p4Yze9-A7-I?si=pIpQdrLtxs0zR07w

video_title: “La Sirenetta” (2023) English Cover | The Little Mermaid Italian Version
description:
Hi everyone! On this 35th year anniversary of The Little Mermaid (1989), I’m so excited to share this English cover of “La Sirenetta”—the Italian version of “Part of Your World” from The Little Mermaid (2023). This cover is a tribute to the brilliant translator, singer, and songwriter Ernesto “Ermavilo” Brancucci, whose creativity has touched the hearts of so many over the years and to the talented Yana_C, the singing voice of Halle Bailey’s Ariel in the Italian dub of the live-action film. It is an honor to bring the beauty of the Italian version of “La Sirenetta” to the English language! 🇮🇹🧜🏽‍♀️🇺🇸

Special thanks to David Mori Romeo for requesting this translation and for helping me adapt Ermavilo’s original Italian lyrics into English. I hope this song holds a special place in your heart as the original does for so many.

What do think of this translation? Do you have a favorite lyric or part of the song?  Do you have a Disney song you’d like to hear retranslated? Let me know in the comments! Here we are all about appreciating the art of audiovisual translation and celebrating the creativity that goes into bringing stories and songs to life in different languages. 😊🌎🎶

Be sure to listen to the original "La Sirenetta" (2023) performed by the one and only Yana_C. Follow her on IG for more music and content @yana_c_official
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c43yQGcfoJY

video_title: Nå Kommer'n (sola) (T-$age Gangster Cover)
description:
Hva om Tore Sagen droppet NRK og debuterte som gangster-rapper i 2003? Dette er “Nå Kommer’n (sola)”, gjenskapt som en hardbarka coverversjon i ekte G-Unit-stil, komplett med AI-stemme, tunge beats og attitude fra Oslo Vest.

🎤 Vokal og produksjon

Dette er en AI-generert cover av “Nå Kommer’n (sola)” fra Papayas univers. Teksten og melodien er den samme, men her tolket med gangster-vri, inspirert av tidlig 2000-talls rap-ikonografi. Stemmen er syntetisk og skapt med kunstig intelligens for å fange tonen til en ny karakter: T-$age, en fiktiv figur basert på en overdrevet og kjærlighetsfull parodi av Tore Sagen.

📸 Bilde og stil

Bildet i thumbnailen er AI-generert og laget for å fremstå som en karikert versjon av T-$age, ikke en realistisk fremstilling av noen ekte person. Med Adidas-drakt, bøttehatt og gullkjede går han rett inn i gangster-arkivet fra 2004, men med et norsk glimt i øyet. Dette er kunstnerisk satire og skal ikke tolkes som en faktisk fremstilling av Tore Sagen.

🧠 Om prosjektet

Dette er en uoffisiell hyllest laget med humor, nostalgi og teknologi. Ingen personer assosiert med Papaya eller PodMe har vært involvert. Det er laget som et eksperiment i AI-generert musikk og satire, gjennom kanalen Gammelt Nytt.

🤍 Hvis du likte dette - abonner, kommenter og foreslå neste AI-cover!

video_title: Lysne - Aksjon På Ål (Hellbillies cover)
description:
Under Cover er ute i dag!

Coveralbumet Under Cover er ute no! Ein samling med 10 låtar som er spelt inn i perioden 2020-2023 då Lysne fortsatt var eit einmannsband, difor er det «gamletrommisen» (han fikk nok, og flytta til Tibet og bytta ut punk med munk)

Her vil du finne låtar du muligens har høyrt før, men denne gong med bedre mix og mastring. Her er alt frå auksjon i Hallingdal til surfing i USA, instrumental Toy Dolls som EGENTLIG er ein 50-talls låt, undervurderte deep cuts frå Raga Rockers og Green Day, + eit par instrumentallåtar på slutten.

SPORLISTE:
Aksjon på Ål (Hellbillies)
Rockaway Beach (The Ramones)
Attitude (The Misfits)
Olga Crack Corn (The Toy Dolls)
Diktator (Raga Rockers)
Big Mouth (The Muffs)
Emenius Sleepus (Green Day)
Murder The Government (NOFX)
DNA (A Flock Of Seagulls)
Til Ungdommen (Otto Mortensen/Trad Arr.)

SPOR 1: «Aksjon På Ål»
Kanskje litt overraskande for mange, men eg ville gjera ein cover av Hellbillies. Denna låten har eg likt veldig lenge, og var vel ein av dei fyrste låtane eg høyrde med bandet. Har lenge tenkt at denna låten må covrast i punkversjon, men det har berre blitt med tanken - heilt te no. Eg skal ikkje gå ut med mine synspunkt på country og populær norsk festmusikk akkurat no, men Hellbillies har alltid våre innafor for meg. Og det har jo såklart ikkje skada at dei med åra har bevegd seg meir mot rocken. Låten var relativt grei å covre. Det stod mellom kjapp californiapunk-takt eller plane Ramones-stil. Sistnevnte funka ikkje heilt, det blei liksom litt traurig. Vokalen var meint å væra litt mørkare, men når låten var ferdig innspilt gikk det litt høgare enn planlagt, men det gikk seg til etter litt øving og vokaltrening. Ein anna utfordring var alle fremmedorda. Dialekten min og halling er vel ikkje dei fjernaste slekningane, men litt utfordringa blei det lell, særlig "sundagsavadelde henn Birgjit", den sleit eg litt med. video_title: Cover Aaron Carter - I'm gonna miss you forever
description:
Protect child stars. Aaron Carter released his first album in 1997 when he was just 10 years old, and the song "I'm gonna miss you forever" was one of my favorites on there. I thought it was so cool that someone only a little older than me was a pop star. 

But my little heart didn't know the cost of that fame, and neither did his. 

Here are some resources if you're struggling: 

https://joingroups.com/  - I've seen Jessica Kent, a person in long term recovery, talk about them a lot, and she also links good resources over on her channel: https://www.youtube.com/c/JessicaKent 

I know access is different in every country, so it's hard to make a good list, but google will show you results relevant to your location. 

And if you know someone who's struggling:

- Educate yourself. Understanding what it is and how it works will be beneficial to you as well as to the person who's in addiction. 
- Get support. You can't carry this alone, and you can't force anyone to get healthy. This takes time, and you'll need support. 
- Don't enable. You can love them without accepting the behavior around you. 
- Take care of yourself. 

You matter. 

----- 

Here's a link to the original music video: I'm Gonna Miss You Forever - Aaron Carter: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jwXxEOTZpvM 

And here's a link to his official YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC8OKGdks56qZ_kPCUV829EQ 


DISCLAIMER: I do not own the rights to the song "I'm gonna miss you forever" by Aaron Carter. This is a tribute cover, in memory of Aaron Carter.

video_title: Grace VanderWaal - Let me hate you (unreleased) COVER
description:
A dear subscriber of mine suggested I give Grace VanderWaal's unreleased song "Let me hate you" a go, so I did, and here's my cover.

Grace VanderWaal is only 17 years old, but she's been writing music for years, performed at countless open mic nights near her home town as a kid, and at age 12 she won the eleventh season of America's Got Talent.

video_title: Indian Sunset - Elton John - Violin Cover by Holly May (Filmed at the Grand Canyon)
description:
Today is Elton John’s birthday 🥳 Elton is my favourite singer and I’m so grateful the past couple of years when in 2022, Elton picked me as one of two winners for his competition to cover his song ‘Cold Heart’ and I got tickets to see his concert in Barcelona 2023 🎶 Me and my family got to see my favourite songs played live and it was incredible ❤️

I chose this song to post today for multiple reasons. I started listening to Elton in December 2019 and so during the lockdown in 2020, I was always searching for and listening to his songs and I came across this one in April 2020 and fell in love with it. 🎼 I think the orchestra is beautiful and I couldn’t wait to perform it once the lockdown was over. I almost got the chance to perform it in June 2020 on a livestream karaoke to our friends and family as someone requested I play it but we didn’t have time. 5 years later, I have never been able to perform it but today I am posting this music video. 🎻

We filmed it last year on 31st March 2024 at the Grand Canyon. I knew I wanted to film two music videos when we visited here because of the stunning scenery and I already had the first song in mind, but when it came to the second song, I had to think. I then remembered about this song I learnt 4 years prior and thought the location would match perfectly 🏜️

I hope you enjoy my violin cover of one of my favourite songs Indian Sunset by Elton John 🎻❤️

Happy Birthday @EltonJohn 🎉

video_title: Lysne - The KKK Took My Baby Away (Ramones cover playthrough)
description:
(FOREIGN VIEWERS: DESCRIPTION IN ENGLISH DOWN BELOW!)

Ramones har eg likt veldig lenge. Det starta med eit bilde som hang på veggen på gutterommet til bror min. Dei hadde skinnjakke, ødelagte olabukser og
rufsete hår. Såg litt merkelig men kult ut. Detta må ha våre på slutten av 90-talet.
Hugsa og eit bilde av Johnny Ramone på ein buss med gitaren i ein bærepose. Det såg så punk ut at eg gjorde det samma.
Eg begynte virkelig å like Ramones sånn i 2000/2001-draget og særlig når Joey døde, det hugsar eg som ein veldig trist dag. Då tok det heilt av med Ramones
for min del. Ein av mine største inspirasjonskilder, og eit av mine desiderte favorittband.
Tok denna låten her som er fra "Pleasant Dreams" plata, som var vel mitt første møte med Ramones eg hadde den på CD.
Håper du liker den! Sjekk gjerne ut min coverversjon av Misfits sangen "Attitude"

video_title: Driver's License Olivia Rodrigo COVER - original key
description:
Super talent Olivia Rodrigo took the world by storm in January 2021, when she released her debut single Driver's License. Critics and regular folks alike were impressed by both her honest songwriting and her belting, and so was I. 
Driver's License has already been covered by the whole internet and their shady uncle, and now it's my turn - in the original key.

I normally write a little about the lyrics and artists in my descriptions, but Olivia Rodrigo is so new to me (I don't have Disney channel) that I don't have much to say. I know there was some love triangle drama - this is a breakup song and she's singing about her ex being "with that blonde girl". I'm not gonna cover that though, I'm here for the music :) 

In this power ballad of a song (classified as bedroom pop and indie pop), Olivia writes about the confusing and conflicting feelings after a breakup - being sad, being angry over lies and feeling deceived, but also still being so in love. It's raw and honest, and probably something most people can relate to. I'm a nerd and love the fact that the title is not in the hook. It's just a simple line at the beginning of the song - I got my driver's license last week - that then sets the backdrop for the story and what the song is really about. 

But yeah. Olivia Rodrigo is insanely talented, she's great with the pen, and I look forward to see more from her over the coming years, that's for sure. 

It's a bit more shouty than what I normally sing (I did it in the original key, only to realize Olivia lowers it a bit live cause she's a smart girl), but I hope you like it. I would NOT be mad if you shared either, that goes for all my videos :) Thank you so much for being her, for watching and supporting me. I realy appreciate you. 

Xx Hege

video_title: No Scrubs TLC cover
description:
When TLC released No Scrubs in 1999, they were already well-known thanks to their 1994 album CrazySexyCool*. But with No Scrubs - the lead single for their third studio album FanMail - they made history by switching up the language and making a feminist anthem.

I adored TLC growing up. They were made up of Tionne “T-Boz” Watkins, Lisa “Left Eye” Lopes (rest in peace), and Rozonda “Chilli” Thomas. Lisa Left Eye Lopes originally had a rap verse on the song, but it was left out from the album version to be able to chart/get played in places that didn't feature rap. But they did release both versions, and many others copied this format as hip hop grew more mainstream. 

* Even though CrazySexyCool did really well, TLC went bankrupt because they had such a bad record deal that they barely saw any of the money it made. video_title: Believe (life after love) Cher COVER
description:
A stripped piano cover of the 1998 worldwide monster hit Believe by Cher. 
Often called "life after love", Believe was one of the first pop songs to use electronically altered vocals in this extreme and obvious way. AutoTune was originally (and still is widely) used for subtle enhancements. The harsher effect we're used to hearing in some genres in today's music was known as the "Cher effect" because of Believe. 

I love the original version of this song. It's a staple in pop music both for the reason mentioned above, and because it's simply a very catchy tune. I chose to do a slow cover of it (to switch it up and) to emphasize the lyrics. Believe is about self-empowerment after a hard breakup. 

Do you believe in life after love? Cher does. 

I also chose to do Believe in a lower key, partly because I found a decent track in that key and partly because I love singing low notes. It said male key, so I was like no.. we can go low too!

video_title: Baby One More Time COVER Britney Spears | Cosplay
description:
...Baby, one more time is Britney Spears' 1998 debut single that became a monster hit and turned Britney into the legend and pop princess that she is. Baby Brit was only 16 years old, what a debut. It might seem weird feeling as much as I do for a pop song with not-so-deep lyrics, but dang.. This song GAVE ME LIFE.

The composition, the tight arrangement, that let's-get-nasty sounding guitar, the backing vocals. It's such a great production.

The theme of the Baby, One More Time lyrics, is that the protagonist is regretting breaking up with their bae. It sparked some controversy back when it was released, because the title line, "Hit me, baby, one more time!" sounds a bit violent and unhealthy. Britney herself said that it "doesn't mean physically hit me. (...) It means just give me a sign, basically. I think it's kind of funny that people would actually think that's what it meant."  

What I find funny about this though, is that the song was written by Swedish Max Martin, and as a fellow Scandi, I can totally see how he meant this in a different way. I love language mess-ups like that, e.g. AHA's "Take On Me", which is a direct translation of the way we say "touch me".

Anyway.. Baby, One More Time was originally intended for TLC and Backstreet Boys, both rejected it. I frikkin ADORE TLC, but I'm so glad this is a Britney Spears song. I wouldn't want the production and sound any other way.

I initially wanted to make my cover very different from the original, maybe with a guitar. Then I realized half of YouTube has already covered this song with a guitar. So.. I chose to go with the sound and version I've loved ever since I was a kid - the original! What I won't do is use the baby voice to try to make it sound like Britney. 

But I WILL dress like her. Consider this my Britney Spears cosplay. (Fun fact: I made the pink scrunchies from a fluffy sock). Let me know if you want more cosplay covers!

video_title: Auld Lang Syne New Year's cover | Hege Official channel Year in Review
description:
Auld Lang Syne is a poem written by Robert Burns in 1788, and set to an old Scottish folk melody. This melody has grown so popular that it's used as a football chant for various teams, a national anthem, and all over the world as a closer for a bunch of different events, most signifying endings or new beginnings. And so, of course, Auld Lang Syne is *the* NYE anthem, and perfect for my channel year in review.

Fun fact/nerd fact! The Auld Lang Syne melody is a pentatonic one, which is one of the reasons it fits matches so many countries' and cultures' common scales. It also makes it perfect for practicing runs. 

I tried my best to cut back on runs and do a simple version to sing along to. But if you're curious as to what the heck a pentatonic scale is, and what it's got to do with vocal runs (or what vocal runs even are), check out this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MOYuMsO8FzA 

I hate the party version, so we're all piano over here (get it? no? comment for help). 

I sing the English version of Auld Lang Syne - often called "old lang syne", "for auld lang syne", or variations thereof. However, the original poem was written in Scottish. I recommend giving Wikipedia's IPA pronounciaton guide for Robert Burns' Ayrshire dialect a go. I tried, but-uh.. 

Anyway, that's enough talk. I just want to THANK YOU for being here with me in 2020. For watching, commenting and liking and making me feel more welcome on YouTube. I really appreciate you. 

So, let me wish you a HAPPY NEW YEAR!! 
And I'll see you in 2021

Take care, stay safe, and have the best start to the new year.

video_title: Needy COVER - Ariana Grande
description:
"Sorry if I'm up and down a lot, sorry that I think I'm not enough, and sorry if I say sorry way too much". These lyrics are too relatable, and I adore this song. Needy is from Ariana Grande's 2019 album, "Thank u, next", and was written by some of my favorites - Ariana Grande, Victoria Monet and Tayla Parx. 

"Tell me how good it feels to be needed". 

We can all feel insecure and in need of emotional support sometimes, and I feel like this is especially true and relevant for a lot of people this year. That's why I decided to cover Needy by Ariana Grande.

I know being needy is frowned upon, and that you should be independent and free in any relationship. And I agree. But I also think it's ok to sometimes feel vulnerable and to want some attention, love and care. And I think that's what Ariana Grande is saying in "Needy". 

In the pre-chorus she also mentions other typically "frowned upon" emotional states. "I'ma scream and shout for what I love, passionate but I don't give no Fs. I admit that I'm a lil messed up (...) I'm obsessive and I love too hard, good at overthinking with my heart". 

It's ok to show emotions, and to be open and vulnerable. And it does feel good to be needed, too - that just means you're important to someone. No one is helped by suppressing their emotions. 

Idk. That's where my head goes with these lyrics. What do you think? 
If you like this video, consider buying me a coffee :) - https://www.buymeacoffee.com/hege 

I hope you're doing well, and that you feel seen and needed just the right way.

Stay safe!

video_title: Fix You COVER - Coldplay // Inspired by Sam Smith
description:
We could all use some healing these days, and Coldplay wrote the perfect soothing lyrics for just that feeling. I've been wanting to cover Fix You for some time now, but seeing Sam Smith performing it inspired me to finally do so.

Check out their version here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ebB1fvJzT24 

And the Coldplay original here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k4V3Mo61fJM 

I decided to do the song in the key Sam Smith (Db instead of Eb) did it, but I forgot how "flat" the song is rangewise. So I recorded the backing vocals first, and when it was time to sing the song, well.. At least I got to train my lower register. 
I always find it hard to keep the energy up on lower songs, so I guess it's a good thing to work on.

Fix You was originally released and performed by Coldplay back in 2005. Sam Smith performed a Fix You COVER just a few weeks go in 2020, and there have been countless other covers of this song over the past 15 years. So why should I bother? Well, cause it gives ME healing just to sing it, and I hope it can do the same for you if you need it.

video_title: Before you go COVER - Lewis Capaldi
description:
Lewis Capaldi wrote Before you go about his aunt, and oh, how I cried hearing the story. The lyric "kills me how your mind can make you feel so worthless" hits so hard, it's difficult to sing it.

I've been wanting to do a 'Before you go' cover for ages now, but I've been putting it off just because it's so emotional. Lewis Capaldi is so good at penning down human experiences and emotions, real feelings that can even be hard to admit. Stuff like "It was never the right time whenever you called, went little by little by little until there was nothing at all" or "I hate you, but I was just kidding myself". Ok I can't. Just go read the story or watch this https://youtu.be/0iBTwBBUYSc?t=71 

I hope you're doing ok. Please know there are people to talk to and resources online if you need someone understanding and/or professional to talk to. You're not alone, there is help.

Take care.

Questa cover K‑pop di “Per sempre sì”, reinterpretata come 너와 나, 영원히 (“Tu e io, per sempre”), trasforma il classico italiano in un brano moderno e coinvolgente per il pubblico globale. Ispirandosi alla versione originale del famoso cantautore italiano, la cover mantiene vivo il tema dell’amore eterno e dell’impegno profondo, ma lo rielabora con arrangiamenti pop‑coreani contemporanei, un ritmo più dinamico, e una produzione tipica del K‑pop con beat elettronici e armonie vocali ricche.

👉 La versione coreana rende omaggio al significato romantico della canzone originale — la promessa d’amore più significativa che una coppia possa fare — interpretandola attraverso melodie luminose, coreografie sincronizzate e una performance vocale intensa che unisce sentimento e energia pop. Sul piano visivo, il video celebra l’unione, l’eternità e la danza come linguaggio universale dell’amore, offrendo sia elementi estetici tipici della cultura K‑pop che la profondità emotiva del testo italiano.

La traccia originale “Per sempre sì” è un inno all’amore duraturo: parla del viaggio di una coppia che supera difficoltà, sogna un futuro insieme e si promette amore eterno — il “sì” più importante della vita. Il testo riflette la volontà di costruire un legame che va oltre le sfide quotidiane, una promessa che unisce le anime in un progetto di vita condiviso.

video_title: Don’t Look Back In Anger - Oasis | Violin Cover by Holly May (Street Performance… in the rain!)
description:
Welcome to my chaotic street performance 😂 it was actually a really lovely day playing for this opticians shop opening but halfway through this song, it started to rain (luckily I was under a little shelter) and the very loud bells started to chime 🎶🌧️🔔 

I actually love the church bells in the city, I just didn’t expect them to start halfway through the song haha 😅 anyway, I hope you enjoy my violin cover of ‘Don’t Look Back In Anger’ by Oasis as the duo recently announced a reunion 🎻🎶

video_title: Barbie Movie Soundtrack Medley on Violin - Holly May Violin Cover (Street Performance) Santa Monica
description:
Today is the one year anniversary of the Barbie movie… I love it so much 😅🩷 So when I went to Santa Monica, I compiled a medley of 4 songs from or related to the Barbie movie soundtrack 🎶 I filmed it when I was at Santa Monica Pier because only a short walk away was Venice Beach (which we visited also) and some famous scenes of the Barbie movie were filmed very close by at Venice Beach so I wanted to have my performance close to it and patiently waited to post it on the anniversary of the movie 😂 I hope you enjoy my violin covers 🩷🎻

During my performance at the pier, it progressively got windier 😅 this was the last song if performance and it was also the windiest so please excuse any mistakes, I was trying my best to hold onto my bow for it not to fly away into the ocean 🤣

Into the Unknown! Frozen 2 Elsa Song (Cover) by Jazzy Skye! This is a Frozen 2 cover song when Elsa wakes up and hears the mysterious voice calling her into the Unknown and away from Arendelle.  The mystery and the call of the voice wakes Elsa and she puzzles out it's meaning and decides to explore.  The magic of the voice awakens and magnifies her powers and she sees the images of the enchanted forest and nature spirits while she sings and explores the intensity of her powers.  Answers and clues to her past and future unfold as the magic and power of her voice and Frozen power dance and sparkle around her.  Will Elsa find who’s behind the voice and discover who is calling her?  Will Elsa be able to tame the nature spirits with her powers? 

Elsa is such an amazing character and so is Anna.  Our kids loved playing these amazing characters in our parodies and skits. In honor of the awesome new “Frozen 2” movie coming out in theaters, we thought it would be fun to do a few Frozen videos for everyone. Kalia is our little Anna, and Jazzy is our Elsa.  Both Kalia and Jazzy had fun recording their voices in "Into the Unknown," "Do You Want to Build a Snowman," "Let it Go."  Even Kade got into the action and will soon release his version of the fun and silly Olaf song, "When I'm Older."  Should we have Jack sing "Lost in the Woods" by Kristoff? What’s your favorite Frozen song?

video_title: Nanmonee/Nannmonee (なんもねえ)  (Norwegian Wasureranneyo (忘れらんねえよ) cover)
description:
I'm sorry in advance for this version!

If you asked me two months ago if I'd do a re-recording of Nanmonee/Nannmonne ( なんもねえ ), the opening song from Yani Neko (Chainsmoker Cat) anime, then the answer would've probably been "I'd consider it" or "No". I was tempted to do a better version as I got more practice with the song, but it felt like I was milking it if I'd just released a re-recorded English version (sorry people who want one that is a little slower...).

But after the release of the English cover, and some discussions in the comment section, I came to realize that maybe I should've gone against the grain and done a Norwegian cover instead, a language that is not so commonly used around the world, and do it in the dialect that I speak, which is somewhat of a less broad version of the "Jærsk" dialect belonging to the south west of Norway (south of Stavanger).

So that is how it came to be. I based the translation to Norwegian on the English translation that I ended up with in my English cover, but as with all translations (now two layers deep), parts of the meaning might change a bit... But I don't think it has changed that drastically from the English translation that I worked with - though it has a bit more swearing. But I have done quite a lot of re-writing on the Norwegian version, trying to find words that would be fitting - and some were pretty hard to find. I'm sure there is someone in the comments that knows Norwegian that could've come up with better words/terms for different aspects of the song. But I rarely write Norwegian lyrics, and I rarely sing in Norwegian... It's natural for speaking, but not so natural for singing.

And I tried to keep it somewhat consistent in speed, though it might speed up a little bit after the "verse". But not as much as the English version (I think?), which got very fast towards the end. 

As for recording, I still kept the same two camera recording setup, but I've started experimenting using the RØDE Wireless Pro ins

video_title: Yani Neko OP in Norwegian (in own dialect) Nanmonee (なんもねえ). Too stupid or should I finalize? #cover
description:
As the video says, I got this "brilliant" idea while interacting in the comment section, that maybe I should've done a Norwegian cover instead of an English one, seeing as English is my secondary language... but I hate singing in the formal-ish way, so I thought I could keep my dialect, which is sort of a cross between Jærsk and Stavangersk.....

Does this deserve to be seen through to the end, or should I just leave it with the English cover I have? 😅 I'm really mixed. 

On one hand, I'd be surprised if there was a Nanmonee cover in Norwegian, and even more so a cover in my dialect... so in that sense it would add something new to Youtube... but then on the other hand, I've already done a cover and I don't want to milk it, even if its a fun song. 

If this early attempt, with pretty early draft Norwegian lyrics, gets received well I might see it through... 🤣

Also, support the original artist: @wasureranneyo.official

description:
I tried to keep the tender nature of the original song, therefore not pushing the vocals too much towards the rougher side, but instead trying to keep it somewhat natural/neutral.

This cover is also the first, in quite a while, that I managed to do in one take - which was usually the idea for these cover songs, to just sit down, press record and play it and upload it as is. The "as is" aspect is still there in all covers, with their flaws and imperfections, but at some point I started doing many takes trying to get it "perfect". But I like the imperfections, the flaws, the rawness of not doing that....

I need to figure out a better way to record the audio for these "live" recordings though (took me 5 takes this time... usually try to stick with one or two tops...). video_title: Dome (milet cover)
description:
Another milet cover - this time from her first album "eyes", the slightly slow and sort-of-dark "Dome", played slightly faster, and kind-of made it my own, like I try to do with most covers while keeping the original very much alive as well. 

Following the same pattern to other covers, that they are just set up the camera and record and whatever comes from it is what it is, as long as the audio is somewhat decent. For this one I used a two cameras and the phone as primary audio device, and mixing the (usable) audio tracks together, but no editing or fancy effects, just that the different microphones picks up different frequencies. I'm trying to keep it as raw as possible.

Been a bit quiet from me lately, but I have a lot of ongoing project that is not music related as well, so it's not always enough time to balance everything out - but there are things happening, even if it's not ready to be published... Just do not know how long it'll take to finish certain new songs.

video_title: Hallelujah//Leonard Cohen **COVER**
description:
Back in 2010 I sat in my neighbours living room with my childhood best. We watched the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympic opening ceremony, and some moments in KD Lang appeared with her short hair, and her white suit, and her fake candle lit crowd, and covered this song like I had never heard before. I thought she had the most incredible voice to pass through that space between my juvenile ears. I downloaded it onto my iPod. Listened to it every day on the bus to my little elementary school. 

I once recorded an acapella version of Hallelujah on this very channel. Most likely shockingly mediocre. (shockingly? expectantly?) Perhaps I'll listen to it one day as it still exists in my private videos somewhere. I have stepped up my GAME since then.. though clearly not enough because I forgot to use a mic.... Whatcha gonna do? It's alright.. it's just a little youtube video. I'm sure I'll cover this many more times in my life. It will never be perfected. I sort of like that this version exists anyway. Worn-out-tired-lownotebarelythere-voice from answering phones all day for my 9-5 work-from-home job. 40 hour-keepsmeafloat-justfornow-maybeforever 9-5 job. emptyroomfullofpeople-alienated-hopelesslyhopeful 9-5 job. I could have recorded another day, but where's the fun in perfection?  Here is where I'm at right now -- or rather two nights ago... when I recorded this.

You’re watching Bjorn Again (Australia), the world’s leading ABBA tribute band, perform Dancing Queen by ABBA — live and loud at Melbourne’s iconic Sidney Myer Music Bowl in March 2024.

Whether you’re 9 or 90, you’ve sung along to this one. It’s been the soundtrack to countless dance floors — and this live performance delivers all the dancing and energy you could ask for, filmed on the very same stage ABBA played back in 1977.

Here’s something for the trivia crowd: Dancing Queen launched in 1976 as the standout single from ABBA’s Arrival album — and it’s been inspiring singalongs and dance moves across generations. Written by Benny Andersson, Björn Ulvaeus, and Stig Anderson, it was recorded at Glen Studios in Stockholm. It’s widely considered ABBA’s most iconic track — the only ABBA song featured on Rolling Stone’s 2004 list of The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time, and inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2015 for its lasting cultural impacts.

Do you know a dancing queen? (Or king?) Share this with them! And don’t forget to like, subscribe, and tap the bell for more ABBA tribute performances from Bjorn Again.

description:
Turns out you can hear the drums, Fernando — and they sound amazing live. Along with the strings, vocals, and everything else that makes this rendition of Fernando by ABBA tribute band Bjorn Again (Australia) one to remember.

Filmed live at Melbourne’s iconic Sidney Myer Music Bowl during the 2024 Moomba Festival — the very same stage ABBA played on back in 1977.

Joining us on stage are the incredible young voices of The Zone Academy’s Children’s Choir, who bring an extra layer of sweetness to this performance. If you caught our video for 'I Have A Dream', you might recognise them — and if not, go check it out! These kids are something special. Link below.

https://youtu.be/6zt-Fhul6M8

Here’s a little backstory for the ABBA fans out there: Fernando was written by Benny Andersson and Björn Ulvaeus, the song’s name was inspired by a bartender the band knew in Stockholm. When ABBA released it in 1976, it became one of their best-selling singles and held the record for the longest-running No. 1 in Australian chart history for over 40 years. It also earned ABBA their first international award: “Best Studio Recording of 1975.”

There was something in the air that night — help someone else see it too. Tell your friends. Tell your group chat. Tell your local bartender named Fernando. — and don’t forget to like, subscribe, and hit the notification bell for more live performances from Bjorn Again.

Break out the tissue box! — world famous ABBA tribute show Bjorn Again brings their heart and soul to this emotional medley of “When All Is Said and Done” and “Slipping Through My Fingers,” filmed live at Melbourne’s iconic Sidney Myer Music Bowl.

These two tracks were included on ABBA's 1981 album 'The Visitors'. 'When All is Said and Done' is an upbeat track featuring Ann-Frid Lyngstad on lead vocal, and 'Slipping Through My Fingers' beautifully sung by Agnetha Faltskog. Both songs explore themes of love, memory, and the passage of time. These touching ballads showcase the depth and sincerity of ABBA’s songwriting, they are true tearjerkers that remind us all to slow down, cherish the little moments, and hold close those who matter most.

description:
Bjorn Again ABBA Tribute Show to play The Sidney Myer Music Bowl in Melbourne Australia on Saturday 9th March 2024. 

This exciting event is commemorating ABBA playing at this same venue on their 1977 Australian Tour. It is also a feature event of Melbourne's Moomba Festival March 7th to 11th 2024.

Bjorn Again is the world’s Number One ABBA tribute band. Formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1988, the band has now toured over 120 countries to international critical acclaim.

Proclaimed as ‘One of the Most Entertaining Show in The World’, Bjorn Again perform all the biggest ABBA hits in a dazzling world class production. At any moment the audience turns into a mosh pit during ‘Dancing Queen’, is dialling imaginary phones in ‘Ring Ring’, is screaming ‘Gimme Gimme Gimme’ at the top of their lungs or crying during ‘I Have a Dream’ or ‘Winner Takes It All’. 

Bjorn Again have performed at Wembley Stadium, The Sydney Opera House and The Royal Albert Hall, at the Glastonbury Music Festival UK and The Big Red Bash in Australia multiple times,  and have performed private shows for Mr Bean (ie Rowan Atkinson) and Bill Gates. Dave Grohl and Metallica are amongst their biggest fans.

video_title: Castle (milet Cover)
description:
A couple of days ago I came across this Milet song and thought it might be a fun song to do a cover of. Many issues with this cover, but it is what it is :-)

Normally I try to keep these covers to a couple of takes, but I kept fumbling up too much on the lyrics so I ended up with six or seven takes, where this was the best of them. My voice was starting to crack towards the end as well, which was why I stopped and went for the best of the takes.

Maybe some way down the road I should do better covers of both of these Milet songs, because they are fun to play and deserve something better than these quick recordings :-)

For those who want to listen to the far superior version (Original): https://youtu.be/KYjWD3sqMmA

video_title: The Love We've Made (milet Cover)
description:
milet's music has been growing on me over the last week, and I figured if I were to cover anything, it would have to be a song that is already fully in english, to avoid having to lean on japanese translations that might not be great - and also having to tweak the translations in order to fit with the singing.

This was the third attempt of recording it. The first two was mostly not used because of incredibly shitty audio, and follows the pattern of most covers I do. Short practice before, and just press record and hope for the best :)

video_title: "Håkon den Gode" - Norwegian Folk song of the Battle of Fitjar - Cover by Jack Wale
description:
"Håkon den Gode" is a Norwegian folk song originally written and sung by the Norwegian folk singer Harald Foss. It recounts in poetic verse the Battle of Fitjar, fought on the island of Stord in western Norway around 961 A.D., between King Håkon the Good and the sons of his late brother, Eirik Bloodaxe.

Håkon the Good was a son of King Harald Fairhair and had spent part of his youth in England at the court of King Æthelstan, earning him the name Håkon Adalsteinsfostre. He returned to Norway and became king during the 10th century, ruling for more than two decades. His reign was marked by efforts to strengthen the organisation and defence of the Norwegian kingdom, as well as his attempts to introduce Christianity to a population which largely continued to practise the traditional Norse religion.

The song focuses upon Håkon's final battle at Fitjar, where the king and his considerably smaller retinue were surprised by a larger force led by the sons of Eirik Bloodaxe. Rather than flee, Håkon and his men chose to stand and fight. Among those accompanying the king was Toralv Sterke Skolmsson, who in the song urges Håkon not to retreat and reminds him that they had overcome greater forces before. Håkon's army ultimately prevailed in the battle, but the king was mortally wounded by an arrow and died shortly afterwards.

Following his death, Håkon was remembered as "the Good", and his life and final battle were preserved in the later Norse saga tradition and skaldic poetry. Most notably, the poem Hákonarmál describes the fallen king being welcomed into Valhalla by the gods, providing one of the most famous surviving literary accounts associated with a Norwegian king of the Viking Age.

Harald Foss is a talented musician who has contributed much to the preservation of Norse and Norwegian history through his music. Many thanks for watching and please excuse any mistakes in translation or pronunciation, as well as the artistic license in the imagery! best wishes to you all.

video_title: "Hvør Skuldi Gamlar Gøtur Gloymt" Auld Lang Syne in Faroese - Cover by Jack Wale
description:
"Auld Lang Syne" is a Scottish folk song that is traditionally sung on New Year's Eve, it expresses themes of friendship, gratitude and nostalgia for good times that have been. It was originally based on an older Scottish folk song obtained and adapted by Robert Burns during his travels which were aimed at preserving the folklore and traditions of the Scottish people following the Act of Union of 1707.

The song was sent by Burns to the Scots Musical Museum in 1788, but was first published with his original additions after his death in 1796. "Auld Lang Syne" was first set to the current melody we know in 1799 by the Scottish music publisher George Thomson, being published in his "Select Songs of Scotland". 

This version is adapted to, and sung in the Faroese language being accompanied by the piano. Please forgive any mistakes that I have made in pronunciation or translation, and if you have any suggestions or requests for future songs, feel free to comment them below! 

Wishing everybody a Happy New Year and the best in 2025. Thank you all for your support. I am greatly looking forward to creating more music and publishing more videos this coming year! God bless you and yours.

video_title: "Merck toch hoe sterck" - Dutch Song of the 80 Years War - Cover by Jack Wale
description:
"Merck toch hoe sterck" is one of the most well known Geuzenliederen of the 80 Years War (referred to in the Netherlands as The Dutch War of Independence), it was written between the years 1622-1625 by the Dutch poet and composer Adriaen Valerius. The setting of the song concerns the relief of the Dutch city of Bergen Op Zoom on the 2nd of October, 1622 after enduring a three month long siege by the Spanish General Ambrogio Spinola and his troops.  The melody of this song is based upon an Elizabethan lute tune written by English composers Thomas Campion and John Dowland in 1606, titled "What if a Day or Month".

Bergen Op Zoom had remained in Anglo-Dutch control since 1588 and successfully repelled repeated Spanish advances and attacks against the city in the following forty years. The city was able to hold out strong during the siege of 1622 due to supply access from the sea on the western side combined with the military deployment of the Scottish Brigade, a British Army unit that was employed in services to the United Provinces throughout the 17th and 18th centuries. On the 2nd of October, Maurice returned triumphantly as the saviour of the city alongside the German commander Peter Ernst II of Mansfeld who forced the Spanish Commander Ambrogio Spinola and his forces to flee.

Please note that the political or religious views of either side of this historic conflict are not condoned. Thank you for watching and please excuse any errors I may have made in pronunciation or production, thank you.

The radio show was called "XL", and aired every weekday for many years back then. The radio show was filmed from inside the studio, and the highlights were shown on TV later, renamed as"XLTV".
The host was Mr. Espen Thoresen, and the guests/singers on this clip are Vibeke Saugestad ("The good singer") and Gunhild Dahlberg ("The less good singer").

Vibeke Saugestad was earlier the lead singer in the rock band "Weld", which had a couple of radio hits in Norway in the 90's. If you like Vibeke's voice, I suggest you check out Weld's two albums, "Natural Tools" and "Hello Walls". The first one being my favorite...

This clip is part of a running gag, which sees Ms. Dahlberg sing karaoke with famous songs, and together with famous Norwegian singers, while having little talent herself for singing.

description:
🎙️ Hva skjer når Luksus Leverpostei møter 60-tallets nattklubb-jazz? “Plastisk Kirurgi” – nå som en 1964-hyllest til skjønnhetsidealer, plastikk og patos. Dette er Gammelt Nytt sin tolkning av Norges mest satiriske låt – forvandlet til en sjarmerende crooner-ballade med varme strykere og et ømt blikk på Botox og selvbilde.

🎧 Vokal og produksjon
Musikk og vokal er AI-generert i ekte lounge-stil – inspirert av Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin og norsk nattklubbstemning anno 1964. Dette er ikke Luksus Leverpostei selv, men en fiktiv parallell fra et røykfylt kabaretscenerom der alt tas litt for alvorlig.

📸 Visuelt uttrykk
Bildet er AI-generert og stilisert som en klassisk jazzplakat fra 60-tallet. Det er ikke en realistisk fremstilling av bandet, men en kunstnerisk hyllest til tidsperioden – med fløyel, whiskyglass og båndmikrofon.

🧠 Om prosjektet
Dette er en uoffisiell hyllest til Luksus Leverpostei. De har ikke vært involvert. Prosjektet er en del av Gammelt Nytt – et eksperiment som tar norske kultklassikere og gir dem nytt (og gammelt) liv gjennom kunstig intelligens og tidsreiser i lyd.

🎤 Original: “Plastisk Kirurgi” – Luksus Leverpostei

video_title: Arne (vintage cover versjon)

Hva om Bare Egil Band ga ut “Arne” i 1957? Dette er en AI-generert vintage-reimagining av den elskede låta, tolket som en soul/crooner-ballade fra gullalderen for live-musikk, varme mikrofoner og røykfylte klubbscener. Her får vi mørke dresser, firestemt bakgrunnsvokal, og én kar med skjegg og stor kjærlighet for Arne.

🎙️ Vokal og produksjon

Alt du hører er laget med kunstig intelligens – vokalen er AI-generert i en klassisk crooner-stil, og musikken er inspirert av amerikansk soul, vokalgrupper og norsk 50-talls dansband. Dette er Gammelt Nytt sin kreative tolkning av sangen “Arne”, laget som en kjærlighetserklæring til både originalen og en musikalsk epoke som aldri helt forlot oss.

📸 Bilde og stil

Thumbnailen og bildet i videon er laget med AI og forestiller en stilisert, uoffisiell versjon av en klassisk vokalgruppe i 1950-årene, der frontfiguren minner om Bare Egil – men er ment som en kunstnerisk tolkning, ikke en realistisk fremstilling. Det visuelle er laget for å matche stemningen i musikken: varmt, teatralsk og tidløst.

🧠 Om prosjektet

Dette er en uoffisiell hyllest. Verken Bare Egil Band eller andre rettighetshavere har vært involvert. Målet er å bruke moderne teknologi til å utforske hvordan klassiske norske låter kunne hørtes ut i en annen tid og en annen stil – uten ironi, men med glimt i øyet.

Abonner gjerne på Gammelt Nytt for flere norske låter i ny (gammel) drakt!

Il mistero del tempo: UN RACCONTO DELLE RAGGED MOUNTAINS (E.A. Poe) 👁️ Song Tribute
description:
🎵 Ascolta "Una storia delle Ragged Mountains", un tributo musicale originale ispirato a uno dei racconti più ipnotici, oscuri e sottovalutati di Edgar Allan Poe: "Un racconto delle Ragged Mountains" (A Tale of the Ragged Mountains, 1844).
Nel cuore delle selvagge montagne della Virginia, il fragile Augustus Bedloe vive un'esperienza che sfida la ragione. Attraverso l'ipnosi del dottor Templeton, i confini del tempo si dissolvono, trascinandolo in un'India del passato, nel bel mezzo di una sanguinosa rivolta. Ma si tratta di una allucinazione dovuta alla morfina, di un esperimento di mesmerismo o di una vera e propria reincarnazione?
Questa canzone ripercorre l'inquietante parallelismo tra Bedloe e l'ufficiale Oldeb (un perfetto anagramma speculare), uniti da un destino fatale e da una morte identica: una ferita alla tempia che squarcia il velo tra passato e presente.
Se ti piacciono le atmosfere gotiche, il mistero e le storie di Edgar Allan Poe, lasciati trasportare da questo viaggio musicale psichedelico e oscuro.
🎧 Stile Musicale: Dark Cyber-Folk / Gothic Rock / Cinematic Synth

video_title: Per sempre sì — Amžinas „Taip“(Sal Da Vinci cover lietuviškai)
description:
„Amžinas Taip“ – tai emocionali itališkos meilės dainos interpretacija lietuvių kalba, sujungianti post-folk, archajiškos muzikos ir elektronikos skambesį. Kūrinys pasakoja apie amžiną meilę, pažadą visam gyvenimui ir dviejų žmonių ryšį, kuris išlieka stiprus nepaisant laiko ir sunkumų.

Tradiciniai lietuviški motyvai susilieja su moderniais atmosferiniais garsais, sukurdami magišką ir kinematografišką nuotaiką. Tai kelionė per meilę, prisiminimus ir Baltijos kultūros dvasią.

Originali daina: „Per Sempre Sì“ – Sal Da Vinci
Lietuviška adaptacija: „Amžinas Taip“

“Amžinas Taip” è un’interpretazione emozionale in lingua lituana di una canzone d’amore italiana, che fonde sonorità post-folk, musica arcaica ed elettronica atmosferica. Il brano racconta l’amore eterno, una promessa per tutta la vita e il legame profondo tra due persone capace di resistere al tempo e alle difficoltà.

Motivi tradizionali lituani si intrecciano con paesaggi sonori moderni e cinematografici, creando un’atmosfera intensa, mistica e coinvolgente. Un viaggio musicale tra amore, memoria e spirito baltico.

Brano originale: “Per Sempre Sì” – Sal Da Vinci
Adattamento in lingua lituana: “Amžinas Taip”

video_title: “Semper Ita (Per Sempre Sì) – Cover Latina Cerimoniale in Stile Antico | Sal Da Vinci”
description:
Carmen hoc, cui titulus est “Semper Ita”, est cantus amoris et promissionis aeternae. Narrat de duobus amantibus qui ab initio ignoto ad coniunctionem perpetuam perveniunt, inter somnia, difficultates et spem futuri. Amor hic non est levis aut caducus, sed firmus atque probatus per adversitates, quae vincuntur communi fide et constantia.

Atmosphaera carminis est sollemnis et quasi nuptialis: vox promittit fidelitatem “usque ad finem vitae” coram Deo, dum verba simplicia — “ita” — significationem aeternitatis accipiunt. Futurum, quamquam incertum, non timetur, quia coniuges simul omnia aedificare volunt sine muris inter se positis.

Hoc carmen igitur celebrat amorem verum, qui non solum in felicitate vivit, sed etiam in certamine confirmatur, atque in una promissione — semper ita — perpetuum vinculum invenit.

Questa canzone, intitolata “Semper Ita”, è un inno all’amore eterno e alla promessa di una vita condivisa. Racconta il percorso di due persone che, da perfetti sconosciuti, arrivano a costruire un legame profondo, fatto di sogni, sacrifici e difficoltà superate insieme.

L’amore descritto non è superficiale, ma forte e autentico: cresce proprio affrontando le sfide e le “salite” della vita. Il momento centrale è quello della promessa, quasi nuziale, in cui i due si giurano fedeltà davanti a Dio, riconoscendo che senza l’altro la vita perderebbe significato.

Nonostante l’incertezza del futuro, i protagonisti scelgono di affrontarlo insieme, senza costruire barriere, accettando anche i conflitti come parte naturale del rapporto. Il semplice “sì” diventa così simbolo di eternità, racchiudendo in una parola tutto il valore di un amore destinato a durare per sempre.

description:
Tok meg ein tur ut på "lokalet" for å teste ut korleis det blir med videopptak.
Å snu mobilen for å få bedre bildekvalitet var nytt for meg. Så der har eg gjort feil heile tiden.
Det er litt ribba på veggane fordi dei ein gong i tiden skulle malast opp igjen, noko som aldri skjedde.
Dei var tapetserte med kule plakatar. Men bakgrunnen skal eg få gjort noko med.
Det er veldig lavt under taket som du ser, det er vanskelig å få gjort noko med.
Tenkte å dra ein kort låt sånn for å teste ut, så eg gikk for ein av dei kortaste sangane eg veit om og ein skikkelig punk rock classic.

"Lokalet" sin historie går langt tilbake i tid, til 90-tallet.
Det er opprinnelig eit pels slaktehus som er gjort om til eit...lokale.
Eg hadde me sofa, bord, TV og kjøleskåp, eg brukte mykje tid der. Hadde PC der eg spilte inn litt demoer (som desverre ikkje har tålt tidens tann og sikkert blitt sletta)
Og det var her at Beinkjør spilte inn deler av "FAEN" albumet.
Etterkvart begynte heavybandet mitt, Norwegian Steel, og øve her, og me spilte inn musikk her. Kjempegøy tid!
Det er rått og kjølig her inne, så plakatane har ikkje tålt tidens tann og var på tide å få ned frå veggane. Skulle male veggene men det blei ikkje noko av.
Uansett, kjekt med litt variasjon i videoane mine, og lyset er perfekt.

Håper du liker videoen, og versjonen. Lik og abboner gjerne på kanalen min det BETYR UTRULIG MYKJE!

This is a coverversion of the song "Murder The Government" originally by NOFX. One of the coolest bands on earth.

video_title: Lysne - Attitude (The Misfits cover playthrough)
description:
Dette er min nye versjon av Misfits klassikeren "Attitude", som eg gjorde ein versjon av i 1999 (link til audiovideo i beskrivelsen), men vokalen og gitaren på den var ikkje akkurat veldig bra, for å sei det forsiktig.
MEN, det er eit fint minne å ha med meg, det var ein morsom opplevelse og ein fin tid.
No, etter alle desse åra, ville eg lage ein ny versjon å sjå korleis det blir i dag.
Originalversjonen til Misfits går i D, min gamle versjon frå 99 er ein plass mellom D og E (gitaren kan ikkje ha våre skikkelig stemt) og denna nye versjonen går i E, standard E-tuning.
Dette blei uansett ein mykje bedre versjon enn den gamle!
Håpa den faller i smak, og det håpa eg videoen gjer og. Der har eg leika meg litt med fargeredigering, så mykje at programmet begynte å lagge såpass voldsomt at eg berre måtte rendre alt å sei meg fornøgd.
Så det blei som det blei.
Kan og nevnast at både sangen og videoen er smelt ihop iløpet av EIN dag.

description:
Royals by Lorde is an anti-luxury anthem, and disapproves of the large and lavish lifestyle represented in a lot of pop and hip hop songs. She explained that the opulence in music videos was far from her reality, and I, for one, can relate.

Lorde's Royals was first released in 2012 as a part of her debut EP, The Love Club EP, which she dropped to SoundCloud where people could listen to it for free. She said it seemed inconvenient for people her age, who likely didn't have access to credit cards, to pay to listen to music. This is very in line with what the Royals lyrics are actually about. 

In 2013, the song was included on Lorde's debut studio album, and was played on the radio all over the world. Royals was a smash and is a timeless bop.

And btw, that "Queen B" meme is just for fun, and no shade to Lorde what so ever. I think it even illustrates the point a bit, cause queens be lavish, and Lorde andher friends are playing that fun without the luxuries.

I hope you like it :) and if you do, a like, a comment or a share really helps your girl out.

Yakan Hikou  (夜間飛行)  (Wasureranneyo (忘れらんねえよ) English cover)
description:
As hinted by in the latest short - a English version of Yakan Hikou (夜間飛行) by Wasureranneyo (忘れらんねえよ) - in my own style.

This translation was based on the one found at Anime Song Lyrics ( https://www.animesonglyrics.com/hajime-no-ippo-rising/yakan-hikou ), in addition to running the lyrics through some translations of different AIs (GPT, and I think Gemini) to try and get the gist of the lyrics in full, and then I did some adjustments and re-writes of the lyrics to make it work with my singing and playing style, while also trying to keep it as true to the original (or as far as I could understand based on the different translations I had at hand). I hope it keeps the feeling and vibe.

Also managed to mess up the video of one of the cameras... so it looks a bit low-res... But oh well...

OP from the anime Hajime no Ippo: Rising, though to be fair, I haven't seen this anime, but I came across (and loved) the song after having discovered the band from Yani Neko's OP: Nannmonee.

Support original artist: ‎⁨@wasureranneyo.official 

If you haven't already, check out the original: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DMJGrmihies

video_title: Hurricane (milet cover)
description:
After some trial and errors I finally managed to do decent enough recording of the newly released milet song - Hurricane. Such an awesome song. 

I was weighing much back and forth if I should sing this with cleaner vocals, or stick with these more raspy vocals, but I think the raspy vocals kinda fit with the theme of the song.

Also tried to not speed it up.... but I did end up speeding the song a bit towards the mid-to-end parts...

As always, check out the original from @miletOfficialYouTubeChannel here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LHoAF3vL8cI

Enjoy (I hope!)!

video_title: Ore yo Todoke  (俺よ届け)  (Wasureranneyo (忘れらんねえよ) English cover)
description:
Here it comes - an English version of Ore yo Todoke (俺よ届け) by Wasureranneyo (忘れらんねえよ).

I did lean heavily on GPT for translating the lyrics, and then I adjusted the results a bit once I felt like I got the gist of the meaning. I hope the translation does the song justice.

Not 100% certain about the chords, but it sounded like it was close-ish most of the time to the song when I was playing along with the original, but there were some parts that were difficult to hear, so I went with gut feeling...

Half of one of the camera recordings I had got corrupted... so after some recovery I at least managed to keep what is in this video... But I did not want to do everything again - so it is what it is.

Also, I'm 10 years late to the party, but this song is incredibly fun (to play and listen to)!

"When it comes to mangas I've read - I won't lose to him!"

Support original artist: ‎⁨@wasureranneyo.official 

If you haven't already, check out the original: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ypCsqWgf8XI

description:
Mamma Mia... Here they go again! Bjorn Again Australia continues to bring the magic of ABBA to life with this performance of “Mamma Mia,” filmed live at Melbourne’s iconic Sidney Myer Music Bowl during the 2024 Moomba Festival. Bjorn Again pulls off a perfect blend of nostalgia and celebration, capturing the timeless energy and playful spirit of the original song.

Recorded at Metronome Studio in Stockholm and released in 1975 on ABBA’s self-titled third album. “Mamma Mia” later became the title track of the beloved musical and iconic film "Mamma Mia!", introducing the song to a whole new generation; who continue to fall in love with ABBA’s music year after year.

Filmed live at Melbourne’s Sidney Myer Music Bowl during in March 2024, this performance took place on the same iconic stage where ABBA performed in 1977, a truly full-circle moment for ABBA fans.

video_title: I HAVE A DREAM - Cover by ABBA Tribute, Bjorn Again
description:
This is Bjorn Again Australia's moving rendition of "I Have a Dream" by ABBA, a timeless anthem of hope and inspiration. Accompanying Bjorn Again on stage are the talented voices of a local children's choir, The Zone Academy, whose voices make this performance truly magical. 

This video was filmed at Melbourne’s Sidney Myer Music Bowl in March 2024 as part of the iconic Melbourne Moomba Festival — the very same stage where ABBA played there in 1977.

ABBA recorded "I Have a Dream" at Polar Studios in Stockholm, Sweden and was released in 1979 as part of the Voulez-Vous album. Its beautiful melody and powerful message of hope have made it a favourite among fans around the world.

video_title: Hurt (Nine Inch Nails / Johnny Cash cover)
description:
This has been a request which I've avoided for such a long time. It's a tough song to do justice because of the original version by NiN, and also the even more powerful version Johnny Cash recorded. So far I've only played it twice for audience (once at a festival around the campfire and the other in a birthday party) and also we did a very different take in a previous band I played in.

But today I was doing some idea recording for new songs, and I was curious how it would sound/look if I filmed myself playing guitar. A much simpler style than before. So it's all very impulsive - one take and stick with it kinda thing. Minor mistakes here and there, but overall decent enough I think. Enjoy.

Swing'it Dixieband presents the sixth video in a serie of Disney covers in 1920's dixieland and 30's swing jazz style! This one is a mix of If I Didn't Have You and the Monsters Inc theme song. This one is a duet between Patrick Williams and Martin Jarl, the horn players in the band, both which are originally piano players. Multitalents, huh?   

The next videos will be out every second Thursday in January and February - so stay tuned! 

Swing'it Dixieband is a Norwegian dixieland band based in London. They've been gigging in London and all over Norway, among others at internationally known festivals like Slottsfjellfestivalen, Molde Jazzfestival and Kongsberg Jazzfestival.

Swing'it Dixieband is a Norwegian dixieland band based in London. They've been gigging in London and all over Norway, among others at internationally known festivals like Slottsfjellfestivalen and Kongsberg Jazzfestival.

The band:
Martin Jarl Velsin - Trumpet, vocals and piano
Patrick Williams - Trombone
Espen Aas - Clarinet
Leon Røsten - Banjo
Double bass - Håvard Mathisen Tanner
Drums - Jeremy Paul
Dancing Bear - Stephan Sykora 

Mixing and recording by Claudi Martinez (http://www.claudimartinez.com/)
Video by Jack Painting

Hymna til Blåfjell is a cover from an old Norwegian children’s TV calendar series in the early 00’s that we millennials used to watch, but the song has been rearranged quite a lot from its original form, with approval from the two composers Bent Åserud and Geir Bøhren.

video_title: Woman interrupts busker with whistle… | Violin Street Performer Holly May
description:
This performance was from last April. For some reason, from February until May last year, I had a lot of trouble every time I went busking, which I’d never had for years and this was one of those moments… I’d already moved busking spots this day because of some trouble at the previous street, and then this woman comes up to me and starts blowing a whistle next to me while I play…? So random 😅 It was funny for the first couple of seconds but then it became really distracting and awkward 😐 Anyway, I hope you can enjoy what was left of my violin cover of That’s What Friends Are For by Dionne Warwick, Elton John, Stevie Wonder and Gladys Knight 🎶 (which was one of my favourite songs to play last summer) 🎻

video_title: Vitas 7th element CHALLENGE #shorts
description:
You know that blblbl-song? Yeah, I want you to try to sing it. Joel from @roomieofficial tried it in a recent video talking about songs that are impossible to sing along to. I had to try too.

If you're not familiar with the blblbl-song, it's called The 7th Element, and it's a song by Ukrainian* singer, Vitas. 

I first came to know about Vitas back in 2010, as Vitas Bumac, when his "Opera #2" went viral the first time around. I was so amazed at his high pitch and how perfectly he managed to transition from a straight note to vibrato, and sound like a soprano. And then the modulations! I was shook, and I've enjoyed and appreciated his talent since.

Vitas, with his playful vocal experimentation and quirky costumes, has made one of the best meme songs there is (in my opinion). Honestly, I'd try to cover the whole song, but-uh.. I'm afraid I'll get the Russian wrong (even though it's one line per verse, repeated). 

I would have filmed this vertically if the video was planned properly. But this is done between takes when I did the Spice Girls - Say you'll be there cover ( https://youtu.be/N9zM81-hf5Q ). I for some reason felt so nervous and weird about filming that day, and needed a fun break. So we watched Roomie Official, laughed at his seagull-edit, and filmed me trying. So it iz what it iz. I hope you enjoy it regardless. 

And join my challenge!! :D Use #vitaschallenge, feel free to include my clip, and let me know in comments if you try. 

Xx Hege

video_title: Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas
description:
Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas was written by Hugh Martin in 1943, for the movie "Meet me in St. Louis", starring Judy Garland, whose character sings this song on Christmas Eve in the film. The song was originally more melancholic than the version we know today, with lyrics about longing for better days. This was, after all, in the middle of WW2, and the song became popular among US troops serving in the war. 

However, the lyrics have been changed a bit for later versions, like the change on Frank Sinatra's version from having to "muddle through somehow" to "hang a shining star upon the highest bough". The idea was to shift the focus to celebrating present happiness, rather than anticipating a better future. 

Countless artists have recorded this song, including Frank Sinatra, Ella Fitzgerald, Luther Vandross, Michael Bublé, Josh Groban and Sam Smith. And tons more have done it live. Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas is a true classic christmas song, and I hope you enjoy my rendition of it. 

Let me know if you do, by hitting that like button and leaving a comment. But most importantly - have yourself a merry little christmas.

video_title: Oh Santa, and the significance of the whistle tone harmony
description:
Ariana Grande and Jennifer Hudson both won the "how it started, how it's going" trend this year, singing alongside Christmas Queen Mariah Carey on a new and rearranged release of her 2010 christmas song, Oh Santa!

I initially wanted to make a reaction video on the music video for Oh Santa, I mean, that whistle tone harmony had me screaming. But I also wanted to discuss an important issue: how media pits women against each other. It's not cute. It splits fans, and creates silly principles, when we could all just enjoy the music that's being put out, that's to our own liking. 

Ariana Grande has been compared to Mariah Carey for years, because they both do whistle notes, for one thing. They have both endured interviewers saying "Ariana's the next Mariah Carey". But Mariah's still here, she's not going anywhere, and they both have so much to bring to the table. In different ways. 

I enjoy and celebrate them both, you don't have to. There's still no need to drag the one that's not your fav. They can both exist and grow, regardless of the other's success. If there's room for all the cis dudes, there's room for all the other people too. 

Oh Santa was the collaboration we all needed to unite fans. Except a few stubborn ones of course. But at least you and me know that they're both talented and worth their space in the music scene. 

If you want more in depth insight on how the media works to make it seem like women are always competing, and how they build them up to make them fall - follow Jameela Jamil on Instagram. She's such a great source for that information. 


Take care, and celebrate the women around you! 

Xx Hege

description:

video_title: 5 Years Of Street Performing Evolution - Holly May Violin
description:

description:
Today, I am posting something much different from what I usually post. 🎻 I mainly only post violin covers on this channel but something else that I love to do is compose original music, so I decided to enter the Indie Film Music Contest 🎶

If you’d like to vote for me in the contest, please like this video 👍

I have never practiced scoring original music for a specific live action video or short film before so it is definitely something new, composing for and creating an orchestra virtually and setting the atmosphere, but I have really enjoyed taking part and setting this short clip to new music! 😊 I hope you enjoy it ❤️🎶

I do not own the copyright to this video clip. This is an original re-score for the film and I only created the music in this video. Original film by Sune Sorensen.

Short write-up about the aim of the music:

It starts off meaning to sound nostalgic with the opening chords played by the strings as he looks back on his life and achievements.

People think he is a bit clumsy and that the lifting weight task is a bit pointless, which is why the music is very 'stop-start' and sounds a bit comedic.
 
As he then looks for hope and inspiration which is heard through the horns and similar chords as the beginning as he reflects.

The music is then more hopeful and uplifting and fast paced as he tries again.

The motif which slightly appeared through the piece develops into the final melody, first with many instruments for harmony as Christmas is a big moment for the little girl but then it simplifies to just flute and oboe as it is a much simpler moment for her Grandad, the special memory between them.

🎵 노래 소개 (K‑Pop Cover)
이 K‑팝 커버 *“Per Sempre Sì”*의 한국어 버전 너와 나, 영원히는 이탈리아의 클래식 명곡을 현대적 K‑팝 스타일로 재해석한 곡입니다. 원곡의 영원한 사랑과 약속이라는 메시지를 그대로 살리면서, 밝고 경쾌한 리듬과 다채로운 보컬 하모니, 현대적인 프로덕션으로 새로운 감동을 선사합니다.

💖 영상에서는 사랑과 연대, 춤과 음악을 통한 감정 표현을 강조하며, K‑팝 특유의 화려한 안무와 시각적 요소로 시청자들에게 깊은 인상을 줍니다.
이 커버는 이탈리아 감성과 K‑팝 에너지의 만남으로, 전 세계 음악 팬들에게 특별한 경험을 제공합니다.

Questa cover K‑pop di “Per sempre sì”, reinterpretata come 너와 나, 영원히 (“Tu e io, per sempre”), trasforma il classico italiano in un brano moderno e coinvolgente per il pubblico globale. Ispirandosi alla versione originale del famoso cantautore italiano, la cover mantiene vivo il tema dell’amore eterno e dell’impegno profondo, ma lo rielabora con arrangiamenti pop‑coreani contemporanei, un ritmo più dinamico, e una produzione tipica del K‑pop con beat elettronici e armonie vocali ricche.

👉 La versione coreana rende omaggio al significato romantico della canzone originale — la promessa d’amore più significativa che una coppia possa fare — interpretandola attraverso melodie luminose, coreografie sincronizzate e una performance vocale intensa che unisce sentimento e energia pop. Sul piano visivo, il video celebra l’unione, l’eternità e la danza come linguaggio universale dell’amore, offrendo sia elementi estetici tipici della cultura K‑pop che la profondità emotiva del testo italiano.

Questa reinterpretazione è perfetta per chi ama sia la tradizione melodica italiana sia l’estetica K‑pop internazionale, creando un ponte musicale tra culture diverse e portando 너와 나, 영원히 nel cuore di spettatori in tutto il mondo.

🎵 Il significato della canzone originale

La traccia originale “Per sempre sì” è un inno all’amore duraturo: parla del viaggio di una coppia che supera difficoltà, sogna un futuro insieme e si promette amore eterno — il “sì” più importante della vita. Il testo riflette la volontà di costruire un legame che va oltre le sfide quotidiane, una promessa che unisce le anime in un progetto di vita condiviso.

video_title: How To Learn A Song By Ear - Holly May Violin
description:
I wanted to learn this ABBA song and I thought I would film and show you how I learn all of my songs by ear. 🎶 

This song took me about 10 - 15 minutes to learn, some songs take 5 minutes and play them in one try, others take 30 minutes to an hour 🎻 

My time learning a song by ear has definitely got faster since I started learning songs like this a couple years ago but the time they take also depends on how well I know a song and if I have heard many times before or not 😅 

I hope you find this video interesting and / or helpful 🎶

PS. This was recorded a couple months ago when I hadn’t got my new violin yet so that I why I am using my old one in the video 😅

video_title: Elton John ‘Farewell Yellow Brick Road’ Tour - Violin Medley (Including Rocket Man, Your Song…) 🚀🎻
description:
Hello everyone! 😃 I am a very big fan of Elton John, and as some of you may know, Elton John’s 5 year long ‘Farewell Yellow Brick Road’ tour came to an end at the weekend. This was Elton’s final tour after performing for over 50 years! 🎶

I attended 2 shows on this tour: 22nd May Barcelona (tickets that I was selected for by Elton from his Cold Heart Cover competition on Instagram last year), and 3rd June Manchester (which was postponed twice since 2020). His shows were phenomenal and I will never forget them! 🚀 

To pay tribute to Elton’s career and final Farewell tour, I have put together a violin medley of 12 covers of my favourite songs from his tour set list - I hope you enjoy! 😄🎻 and let me know in the comments, what is your favourite Elton John song? 🎵

Elton John Violin Medley - Song Order:

1. Bennie And The Jets
2. Crocodile Rock
3. Love Lies Bleeding 
4. Have Mercy On The Criminal
5. Tiny Dancer
6. Philadelphia Freedom
7. I Guess That’s Why They Call It The Blues
8. Someone Saved My Life Tonight
9. Your Song
10. Rocket Man
11. I’m Still Standing
12. Goodbye Yellow Brick Road

video_title: My 4 Year Violin Progress
description:
Hi everyone! This is my 4 year violin progress video - I hope you enjoy it 😊🎻

I used to play violin when I was younger but I never practiced and became very un-motivated and so I quit. About 4 years ago, I started to play again, self-taught learning pop songs using a mixture between violin tabs on YouTube and learning by ear 🎶 I got a teacher in March 2021, who I have weekly online lessons with to work on classical music 🎼 

I now love to play violin and I’m so happy that I picked it back up again as I’m now hoping to have violin and music as my career. 🎻

Thank you so much for all of the support on my YouTube channel - over the years, your support has really encouraged me to practice and continue making covers and music 🙏😄🎻
